--- title: "K12Enrollment" editor: visual --- # Data prep This dataset is of all the individuals that have graduated from a high school in Northeast Minnesota.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} enrollment.original <- read_csv('/Users/kellyasche/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-kasche@ruralmn.org/My Drive/Research/FY25-27/FY27/OHE Journey to meaningful employment/Data/CRPD 2 (angelique.workman@state.mn.us)/K12Enrollment.csv') %>% mutate(PersonID = as.integer(PersonID), K12OrganizationID = as.integer(K12OrganizationID)) %>% drop_na(PersonID) kable(head(enrollment.original)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | PersonID| K12OrganizationID| TimeID| Grade| EconomicStatusIndicator|FederalRaceIndicator |PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator |PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator | RaceEthnicity| StatusEnd|Gender | SpecialEdStatus|LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator | HomePrimaryLanguage|HomelessIndicator | |--------:|-----------------:|--------:|-----:|-----------------------:|:--------------------|:---------------------------------------|:---------------------------------|-------------:|---------:|:------|---------------:|:----------------------------------|-------------------:|:-----------------| | 11184140| 136348| 20070630| 11| 1|NA |N |NA | 5| 40|M | 1|N | 11|N | | 2008451| 137653| 20070630| 12| 0|NA |N |NA | 5| 8|F | 1|N | 11|N | | 9316370| 67446| 20070630| 11| 0|NA |N |NA | 5| 40|F | 1|N | 11|N | | 549086| 70522| 20080630| 11| 0|NA |N |NA | 5| 40|M | 1|N | 11|N | | 1439556| 22668| 20120630| 12| 2|H |N |N | 3| 8|M | 1|N | 45|N | | 5905086| 12277| 20120630| 11| 1|W |N |N | 5| 40|M | 1|N | 11|N | ::: ```{.r .cell-code} kable(names(enrollment.original)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:---------------------------------------| |PersonID | |K12OrganizationID | |TimeID | |Grade | |EconomicStatusIndicator | |FederalRaceIndicator | |PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator | |PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator | |RaceEthnicity | |StatusEnd | |Gender | |SpecialEdStatus | |LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator | |HomePrimaryLanguage | |HomelessIndicator | ::: :::
In the dataset there are 2,121,377 observations along with 15 columns. Each observation does not represent a unique, unduplicated individual, but rather a unique status for the individual. For example, one individual can have multiple observations if they changed schools, for each school year, or if their economic status changed in the middle of a school year. Next we need to create a dataset that only has students who graduated from a high school located in the Southwest research region - EDRs 6W, 6E, and 8. To do that, we will need to join up with the organization spreadsheet.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} k12.org.original <- read_csv('/Users/kellyasche/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-kasche@ruralmn.org/My Drive/Research/FY25-27/FY27/OHE Journey to meaningful employment/Data/CRPD 2 (angelique.workman@state.mn.us)/K12Organization_cleaned.csv') %>% distinct(K12OrganizationID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% drop_na(K12OrganizationID) %>% mutate(K12OrganizationID = as.integer(K12OrganizationID)) %>% group_by(NCESID) %>% fill(SiteCountyCode, .direction = "downup") %>% ungroup() kable(head(k12.org.original)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | K12OrganizationID| DistrictID| SchoolNumber| StateOrganizationID| StateFiscalYear| NCESID|OrganizationName | UnitClassification|AddressType |City | SiteCountyCode| |-----------------:|----------:|------------:|-------------------:|---------------:|----------:|:-----------------|------------------:|:-----------------|:-------|--------------:| | 2298| 122| 2| 1.0253e+10| 2005| 2.7129e+11|GOODHUE SECONDARY | 33|MAILING |Goodhue | 25| | 2299| 122| 2| 1.0253e+10| 2006| 2.7129e+11|GOODHUE SECONDARY | 33|MAILING |Goodhue | 25| | 2300| 122| 2| 1.0253e+10| 2007| 2.7129e+11|GOODHUE SECONDARY | 33|MAILING |Goodhue | 25| | 2301| 122| 2| 1.0253e+10| 2008| 2.7129e+11|GOODHUE SECONDARY | 33|PHYSICAL_LOCATION |Goodhue | 25| | 2302| 122| 2| 1.0253e+10| 2009| 2.7129e+11|GOODHUE SECONDARY | 33|MAILING |Goodhue | 25| | 2303| 122| 2| 1.0253e+10| 2010| 2.7129e+11|GOODHUE SECONDARY | 33|MAILING |Goodhue | 25| ::: ```{.r .cell-code} kable(names(k12.org.original)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:-------------------| |K12OrganizationID | |DistrictID | |SchoolNumber | |StateOrganizationID | |StateFiscalYear | |NCESID | |OrganizationName | |UnitClassification | |AddressType | |City | |SiteCountyCode | ::: :::
This dataset provides each school institution as of June 29, 2024. This isn't a list of each school but rather a list of each K12OrganizationID. Each school will have multiple K12OrganizationID. I'm not sure why and this would be something to ask Meredith. In addition, there are a lot of county codes missing. So I'm going to use the listed city to try and clean that up. My goal is to join my standardized region and county code data with this document which will then be joined to the master enrollment document. Unfortunately the main data does not include county name but rather their own code for county. So I will join their codes with the county names and then use my counties.regions data to bring together the remaining regions.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} SiteCountyCode <- read_csv("~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-kasche@ruralmn.org/My Drive/Research/FY25-27/FY27/OHE Journey to meaningful employment/Data/SiteCountyCodes.csv") k12.org.master <- k12.org.original %>% left_join(SiteCountyCode[,c(1,2)], by = c("SiteCountyCode" = "Code")) %>% drop_na(SiteCountyCode) %>% rename(county.name = `Code definition`) %>% select(K12OrganizationID, OrganizationName, county.name) %>% mutate(county.name = str_replace(county.name, " County", ""), county.name = str_replace(county.name, "Saint Louis", "St. Louis")) %>% filter(county.name != "Unknown") %>% select(K12OrganizationID, OrganizationName, county.name) %>% left_join(counties.regions.1, by = c("county.name" = "Name")) %>% select(-Dem_RUCA, -mif, -edr.simple) kable(head(k12.org.master)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | K12OrganizationID|OrganizationName |county.name |countyfp |Dem_Desc |edr |planning.region |statefp | |-----------------:|:-----------------|:-----------|:--------|:--------------------|:------------------|:---------------|:-------| | 2298|GOODHUE SECONDARY |Goodhue |049 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 10 - Southeast |Southern |27 | | 2299|GOODHUE SECONDARY |Goodhue |049 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 10 - Southeast |Southern |27 | | 2300|GOODHUE SECONDARY |Goodhue |049 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 10 - Southeast |Southern |27 | | 2301|GOODHUE SECONDARY |Goodhue |049 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 10 - Southeast |Southern |27 | | 2302|GOODHUE SECONDARY |Goodhue |049 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 10 - Southeast |Southern |27 | | 2303|GOODHUE SECONDARY |Goodhue |049 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 10 - Southeast |Southern |27 | ::: ```{.r .cell-code} kable(names(k12.org.master)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:-----------------| |K12OrganizationID | |OrganizationName | |county.name | |countyfp | |Dem_Desc | |edr | |planning.region | |statefp | ::: :::
Now I should be able to join this dataset with the enrollment data to figure out what EDR they are from and then filter any rows that are not associated with a school district located in EDR 3.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} enrollment.org.sw <- enrollment.original %>% left_join(k12.org.master, by = "K12OrganizationID") %>% select(-statefp) %>% filter(planning.region == "Southwest") kable(head(enrollment.org.sw)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | PersonID| K12OrganizationID| TimeID| Grade| EconomicStatusIndicator|FederalRaceIndicator |PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator |PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator | RaceEthnicity| StatusEnd|Gender | SpecialEdStatus|LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator | HomePrimaryLanguage|HomelessIndicator |OrganizationName |county.name |countyfp |Dem_Desc |edr |planning.region | |--------:|-----------------:|--------:|-----:|-----------------------:|:--------------------|:---------------------------------------|:---------------------------------|-------------:|---------:|:------|---------------:|:----------------------------------|-------------------:|:-----------------|:-------------------------------|:---------------|:--------|:--------------------|:------------------------------|:---------------| | 1439556| 22668| 20120630| 12| 2|H |N |N | 3| 8|M | 1|N | 45|N |LAKEVIEW SECONDARY |Lyon |083 |Town/rural mix |EDR 8 - Southwest |Southwest | | 5536182| 182741| 20190630| 10| 0|H |N |N | 0| 40|F | 1|N | 45|N |WILLMAR SENIOR HIGH |Kandiyohi |067 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6E- Southwest Central |Southwest | | 10551433| 111252| 20160630| 11| 0|W |N |N | 5| 20|M | 1|N | 11|N |Montevideo Senior High |Chippewa |023 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6W- Upper Minnesota Valley |Southwest | | 2572031| 204333| 20220630| 12| 2|B |N |N | 0| 4|M | 4|N | 11|N |WILLMAR SENIOR HIGH |Kandiyohi |067 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6E- Southwest Central |Southwest | | 2522562| 184724| 20200630| 11| 1|W |N |Y | 0| 40|F | 1|N | 11|N |CANBY SECONDARY |Yellow Medicine |173 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6W- Upper Minnesota Valley |Southwest | | 9604960| 182420| 20190630| 10| 0|W |N |N | 0| 99|F | 1|N | 11|N |GLENCOE-SILVER LAKE SENIOR HIGH |McLeod |085 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 6E- Southwest Central |Southwest | ::: ```{.r .cell-code} kable(names(enrollment.org.sw)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:---------------------------------------| |PersonID | |K12OrganizationID | |TimeID | |Grade | |EconomicStatusIndicator | |FederalRaceIndicator | |PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator | |PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator | |RaceEthnicity | |StatusEnd | |Gender | |SpecialEdStatus | |LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator | |HomePrimaryLanguage | |HomelessIndicator | |OrganizationName | |county.name | |countyfp | |Dem_Desc | |edr | |planning.region | ::: :::
The dataset now has 216,240 instances that provide a number of characteristics about an individuals enrollment. My goal is to end up with a dataset where each observation (row) represents a unique (unduplicated) individual that's tied to the school from which they graduated. Here's how I will do that. - PersonID: change to integer - K12OrganizationID: change to integer. - K12EnrTimeID: Change so it's only the year - Grade: eliminate - unimportant since we are mostly concerned about whether they graduated. - EconomicStatusIndicator: I will change this to two categories. Whether they were ever eligible for reduce priced or free meal will be coded as 1 (eligible = codes 1, 2, 4, 5) at any point in the dataset. The remaining will be coded as 0. - FederalRaceIndicator: eliminate - I'm going to use the RaceEthnicity column instead. - PSEO columns: I'm most concerned about whether they participated in PSEO or not. A new column will be created indicated whether there was a "Y" coded for either the "PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator" or "PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator" columns at any point in the dataset. The two original columns will be eliminated. - StatusEnd: I will only include individuals that have StatusEnd coded as an 8 or 9. - Gender: included and not changed. - SpecialEdStatus: I will split this into two categories. The first is that a student did not require special education services (codes 1-2) at any point in the dataset. The other category will be that they require special education (codes 4 - 9) at any point in the dataset. - Limited English: keep with no changes. - Primary language: I'm going to create two categories. One being that English is the primary language while the other will be that English is NOT the primary language at any point in the dataset. - Homeless: Keep with no changes. We first need to create a list of all individuals with the StatusEnd code of 8 or 9 (graduated). In addition, we need to remove any student that graduated before 2008. This is because we will not have their full Sophmore - Senior records which is especially important when attempting to identify whether the number of CTE courses taken predicts migration. The other element I want to add is a pre-covid and post-covid variable. All individuals whose grad year is before 2020 will be labeled pre-covid and all others wil lbe post-covid. This "graduates list" will be the list on which we will bind all the other variables.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} graduates <- enrollment.org.sw %>% filter(StatusEnd %in% c(8,9)) %>% mutate(grad.year = str_sub(TimeID, 1, 4), grad.year = as.integer(grad.year), grad.year.covid = ifelse(grad.year > 2019, "Post-covid grad", "Pre-covid grad")) %>% select(PersonID, K12OrganizationID, OrganizationName, grad.year, grad.year.covid, Gender, LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator, HomelessIndicator, county.name, countyfp, Dem_Desc, edr, planning.region) %>% distinct(PersonID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% filter(grad.year > 2007) ``` :::
Next we need to create new columns for the variables that will indicate a certain status has been met at any point in the dataset for each PersonID. For example, we want a column that indicates a PersonID was enrolled in PSEO at some point in the dataset. The variables that need a new column created are; - EconomicStatusIndicator - PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator & PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator - SpecialEdStatus - HomeprimaryLanguage
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Lets start with economic status indicator k12.enr.esi.indicator <- enrollment.org.sw %>% select(PersonID, EconomicStatusIndicator) %>% group_by(PersonID) %>% mutate(economic.status.code = ifelse(EconomicStatusIndicator %in% c(1,2,4,5), 1, 0), economic.status.code.sum = sum(economic.status.code)) %>% ungroup() %>% distinct(PersonID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% mutate(economic.status = ifelse(economic.status.code.sum > 0, 1, 0)) %>% select(PersonID, economic.status) # PSEO k12.enr.pseo.indicator <- enrollment.org.sw%>% select(PersonID, PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator, PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator) %>% mutate(PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator = ifelse(PostSecondaryEnrollmentOptionsIndicator == "Y", 1, 0), PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator = ifelse(PSEOConcurrentEnrollmentIndicator == "Y", 1, 0)) %>% gather(key = "pseo.type", value = "indicator", 2:3) %>% group_by(PersonID) %>% summarise(pseo = sum(indicator)) %>% mutate(pseo.participant = ifelse(pseo > 0, 1, 0)) %>% ungroup() %>% select(PersonID, pseo.participant) # Special Ed status k12.enr.spced.indicator <- enrollment.org.sw %>% select(PersonID, SpecialEdStatus) %>% mutate(SpecialEdStatus.code = ifelse(SpecialEdStatus %in% c(4,5,6,7,8,9), 1, 0)) %>% group_by(PersonID) %>% summarise(SpecialEdStatus.sum = sum(SpecialEdStatus.code)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(SpecialEdStatus = ifelse(SpecialEdStatus.sum > 0, 1, 0)) %>% select(PersonID, SpecialEdStatus) # Home Primary Language k12.enr.homeprimlang.indicator <- enrollment.org.sw %>% select(PersonID, HomePrimaryLanguage) %>% mutate(HomePrimaryLanguage.code = ifelse(HomePrimaryLanguage == 11, 0, 1)) %>% group_by(PersonID) %>% summarise(HomePrimaryLanguage.sum = sum(HomePrimaryLanguage.code)) %>% ungroup() %>% mutate(non.english.home = ifelse(HomePrimaryLanguage.sum > 0, 1, 0)) %>% select(PersonID, non.english.home) # Race k12.enr.race <- enrollment.org.sw %>% select(PersonID, RaceEthnicity) %>% mutate(RaceEthnicity = ifelse(RaceEthnicity == 0, "Unknown", ifelse(RaceEthnicity == 1, "AI", ifelse(RaceEthnicity == 2, "Asian/PI", ifelse(RaceEthnicity == 3, "Hispanic", ifelse(RaceEthnicity == 4, "Black", "White"))))), RaceEthnicity = as.factor(RaceEthnicity)) %>% distinct(PersonID, RaceEthnicity) %>% mutate(code = ifelse(RaceEthnicity == "Unknown", 0, 1)) %>% group_by(PersonID) %>% filter(code == max(code)) %>% ungroup %>% distinct(PersonID, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% select(PersonID, RaceEthnicity) ``` :::
Now we can combine the list of graduates with the status indicators.
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} k12.enrollment.master <- graduates %>% left_join(k12.enr.esi.indicator, by = "PersonID") %>% left_join(k12.enr.pseo.indicator, by = "PersonID") %>% left_join(k12.enr.spced.indicator, by = "PersonID") %>% left_join(k12.enr.homeprimlang.indicator, by = "PersonID") %>% left_join(k12.enr.race, by = "PersonID") %>% select(PersonID, K12OrganizationID, OrganizationName, county.name, countyfp, Dem_Desc, edr, planning.region, grad.year, grad.year.covid, Gender, LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator, HomelessIndicator, economic.status, pseo.participant, SpecialEdStatus, non.english.home, RaceEthnicity) kable(head(k12.enrollment.master)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} | PersonID| K12OrganizationID|OrganizationName |county.name |countyfp |Dem_Desc |edr |planning.region | grad.year|grad.year.covid |Gender |LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator |HomelessIndicator | economic.status| pseo.participant| SpecialEdStatus| non.english.home|RaceEthnicity | |--------:|-----------------:|:-------------------------------|:---------------|:--------|:--------------------|:------------------------------|:---------------|---------:|:---------------|:------|:----------------------------------|:-----------------|---------------:|----------------:|---------------:|----------------:|:-------------| | 1439556| 22668|LAKEVIEW SECONDARY |Lyon |083 |Town/rural mix |EDR 8 - Southwest |Southwest | 2012|Pre-covid grad |M |N |N | 1| 0| 0| 1|Hispanic | | 9507055| 47654|GLENCOE-SILVER LAKE SENIOR HIGH |McLeod |085 |Urban/town/rural mix |EDR 6E- Southwest Central |Southwest | 2008|Pre-covid grad |F |N |N | 0| NA| 0| 0|White | | 9657752| 155404|E.C.H.O. CHARTER SCHOOL |Yellow Medicine |173 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6W- Upper Minnesota Valley |Southwest | 2009|Pre-covid grad |M |N |N | 1| NA| 1| 0|Hispanic | | 8919833| 111262|MONTEVIDEO SENIOR HIGH |Chippewa |023 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6W- Upper Minnesota Valley |Southwest | 2013|Pre-covid grad |F |N |N | 1| 0| 0| 0|White | | 1594136| 195989|BENSON AREA LEARNING CENTER |Swift |151 |Town/rural mix |EDR 6W- Upper Minnesota Valley |Southwest | 2021|Post-covid grad |M |N |N | 1| 0| 1| 0|Unknown | | 7207828| 195845|RTR HIGH SCHOOL |Lincoln |081 |Entirely rural |EDR 8 - Southwest |Southwest | 2021|Post-covid grad |F |N |N | 1| 1| 0| 0|Unknown | ::: ```{.r .cell-code} kable(names(k12.enrollment.master)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |x | |:----------------------------------| |PersonID | |K12OrganizationID | |OrganizationName | |county.name | |countyfp | |Dem_Desc | |edr | |planning.region | |grad.year | |grad.year.covid | |Gender | |LimitedEnglishProficiencyIndicator | |HomelessIndicator | |economic.status | |pseo.participant | |SpecialEdStatus | |non.english.home | |RaceEthnicity | ::: ```{.r .cell-code} write_csv(k12.enrollment.master, "Data/SLEDS/K12 Enrollment/K12Enrollment-master.csv") ``` :::
The prepped enrollment data has 54,063 observations and 18 columns.
# Summary of K12Enrollment data Below is the percentage of total observations that; - Were eligible for free or reduced lunch at some point in the dataset - Are Female - Have been homeless at some point in the dataset - Had limited english proficiency at some point in the dataset - Had non english speakders in home at some point in the dataset - Participated in a PSEO course at some point in the dataset. - Pct non white As expected, nearly half (49.2%) of the observations are female. Over a third (37%) of the observations have been eligible for free or reduced lunch at some point in the dataset. Also, over a third (33.4%) of observations participated in a PSEO course. There is a large percentage identifying as non-white with 34.1%, while 13.8% were categorized as needing special education, 10% with a non-english speaker in the home, 2.9% with limited english proficiency and 0.5% homeless.
